stratified_examples.question: I need to update the og:image for my entire site to ensure the correct image appears when the link is posted on social media. I also want to know if this will affect the image when the link is posted in an email or on Instagram.
stratified_examples.candidate_answer:
To update the og:image for your entire site on Wix:

- Go to your site's settings.
- Click Website settings.
- Scroll down to General social image and click Upload Image.
- Select or upload the desired image.
- Click Choose File, then Save at the top of the dashboard.
- Publish your site to apply changes [S1].

Regarding the impact on other platforms:

- The og:image primarily controls the thumbnail image shown when your site link is shared on social media platforms like Facebook and X.
- For email clients and Instagram, the display of link previews varies and may not always use the og:image tag consistently. Instagram, for example, often does not generate link previews with images.
- Therefore, updating the og:image ensures correct social media sharing thumbnails but may not guarantee the same image appears in email previews or Instagram posts.

Ensure your og:image follows the recommended aspect ratio of 1.91:1 to avoid cropping issues [S1].

In summary:
- Updating the og:image affects social media link previews.
- Email and Instagram may not reliably use the og:image for link previews.

stratified_examples.question: Im unable to access the Google Maps element in the footer of my Wix site. Im having trouble removing it, and I dont know where the overlapping items feature is located.
stratified_examples.candidate_answer:
To access and remove the Google Maps element in your Wix site's footer when it's overlapped by other elements, follow these steps:

- Open the Layers panel in the Wix Editor by clicking the Layers icon at the bottom of the editor. This helps locate the Google Maps element if it is behind other elements or outside the gridlines.
- Use the Overlapping Items feature by right-clicking on the element that is covering the Google Maps element. Then, hover over "Overlapping Items" in the context menu and select the Google Maps element from the list.
- If you still cannot select it, right-click the covering element, hover over "Arrange," and choose "Move Backward" repeatedly until the Google Maps element becomes accessible.
- Alternatively, use the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Shift + M (Cmd + Shift + M on Mac) to toggle through elements on the page until you reach the Google Maps element.

These steps will allow you to select and remove the Google Maps element from the footer effectively [S1][S2].

4. Find the relevant element on the list and click to select it.

If you see an element on your live site or in Preview mode, but not in the editor, it might be placed outside of the site's gridlines. Toggle through your page elements to locate the element.

1. Hold down Ctrl (Cmd on Mac) + Shift on your keyboard.
2. Press M to scroll through the elements on your site until you reach the desired element.
